title: ML Workflow, Math's Role, Ethics & the Future of AI
description: Mixed-format quiz (MCQ, true/false, select-all) on the end-to-end Machine Learning workflow, the role of mathematics in ML, how data quality affects models, ethical issues in AI, and the future scope of AI/ML — aligned with the university question bank (Q70–Q74).

questions.question: In the end-to-end ML workflow, which stage comes immediately after "Data collection"?
Which stage of the ML workflow involves dividing data into training, validation, and testing sets, possibly using cross-validation?
In the ML workflow, what does the "Training" stage involve?
options: Allowing the model to learn patterns from the training data using gradient-based optimization
Cleaning missing values from the raw dataset
Deploying the finished model into production
questions.answer: Allowing the model to learn patterns from the training data using gradient-based optimization

questions.question: Why is "Deployment and monitoring" treated as an ongoing responsibility rather than a one-time final step?
options: Because real-world data can drift away from the training data's patterns over time
Because deployed models are never evaluated again under any circumstances
Because monitoring must happen before any data is ever collected
Because deployment always occurs before model training
questions.answer: Because real-world data can drift away from the training data's patterns over time

questions.question: Which branch of mathematics enables data to be represented and transformed as vectors and matrices, and underlies every calculation inside a neural network layer?
Which mathematical concept, drawn from calculus, describes exactly how a model's parameters should be adjusted to reduce error during training?
What principle is often summarized as "garbage in, garbage out" in the context of Machine Learning models?
options: A model's performance is fundamentally limited by the quality of the data it is trained on
Models always perform best when trained on the smallest possible dataset
Data quality has no measurable effect on model performance
Only the choice of algorithm matters, never the underlying data
questions.answer: A model's performance is fundamentally limited by the quality of the data it is trained on

questions.question: How can missing values in training data affect a model?
options: They can bias the model toward the records that happen to be complete
They always improve the model's overall accuracy
They have no possible effect on model performance
They only ever affect unsupervised learning models
questions.answer: They can bias the model toward the records that happen to be complete

questions.question: What can happen if a model's training data contains societal or historical bias?
options: The model can learn and even amplify that bias, leading to unfair or discriminatory outcomes
The model automatically detects and removes the bias on its own
Bias in training data only ever affects unsupervised learning tasks
Bias in the data has no effect whatsoever on the model's predictions
questions.answer: The model can learn and even amplify that bias, leading to unfair or discriminatory outcomes

questions.question: Which ethical concern refers to the difficulty of understanding or explaining how a complex model, such as a deep neural network, arrives at its decisions (the "black box" problem)?
Which ethical concern involves determining who is responsible when an AI system makes a harmful or incorrect decision?
Which of the following is a growing future direction in AI, aimed directly at addressing the "black box" transparency problem?
An insufficient quantity of training data can prevent a model from learning a pattern reliably, potentially leading to underfitting.
Statistics and probability provide the tools to summarize data and reason about uncertainty formally.
Handling personal or sensitive data, such as medical records, requires no special safeguards, since Machine Learning models are private by default.
A model that performs perfectly on its training data but generalizes poorly to new, unseen data is, for practical purposes, not considered a useful model.
Which of the following are stages of the end-to-end ML workflow?
Which branches of mathematics are described as foundational to building ML models?
Which of the following are ethical issues in AI and Data Science?
Which of the following are emerging future directions for AI and ML?
options: More data-efficient learning methods that need less labeled data
The complete elimination of all computing hardware
answer: More data-efficient learning methods that need less labeled data
